summary: The note describes the 1973 Chilean coup d'état as a watershed event in Chilean history and the Cold War. It explains that the coup followed a period of social unrest and political tension between the opposition-controlled Congress and socialist President Salvador Allende, along with economic warfare ordered by US President Richard Nixon. Allende was overthrown by the armed forces and national police.
one_line: Overview of the 1973 military coup that overthrew Chilean President Salvador Allende, amid Cold War tensions and US-ordered economic warfare.
key_facts: The 1973 Chilean coup d'état was described as a watershed moment in both the history of Chile and the Cold War.
The coup followed an extended period of social unrest in Chile.
There was political tension between the opposition-controlled Congress of Chile and the socialist President Salvador Allende.
Economic warfare was ordered by US President Richard Nixon against Chile.
Salvador Allende was overthrown in the 1973 coup.
The coup was carried out by the armed forces and national police.
The opposition controlled the Congress of Chile at the time of the coup.
Salvador Allende was a socialist president of Chile.
